content:
frank: quick callout - ran into a subtle parity issue in the sampleapp Go + CLI flow for rerank/embeddings. Repro consistently when batch size >= 6 and one shard falls back.

frank: Repro (Go sampleapp):
```go
// send_batch.go (go-sdk v0.4.1)
ids := make([]string, len(docs))
vecs := make([][]float64, len(docs))
for i,d := range docs {
  ids[i] = d.ID
  vecs[i] = padVec(d.Vector, 256) // model expects 256
}
resp, err := client.Rerank.Batch(ctx, model, BatchBody{Ids: ids, Vectors: vecs})
```

frank: Symptom: after a retry cascade we see correct scores but the Go helper zips scores to original order by index and attaches `metadata` by index. If runtime returns `result_ids` in a different order the UI shows wrong doc->snippet associations.

anya: can you paste the server log + raw response?

frank: server snippet: 
```
[2026-12-14T20:12:01Z] incoming batch id=batch-119 size=8 client=go-0.4.1
[2026-12-14T20:12:01Z] dispatch shard=rerank-7 seq=754
[2026-12-14T20:12:02Z] model timeout seq=754
[2026-12-14T20:12:02Z] fallback dispatch shard=rerank-2 seq=754 retry=1
[2026-12-14T20:12:03Z] response sent seq=754 idempotency=missing order_preserved=false
```

frank: response body (trim):
```
{ scores:[0.94,0.78,0.64,0.51,0.28,0.12,0.05,0.01], result_ids:["doc-2","doc-0","doc-5","doc-4","doc-1","doc-3","doc-7","doc-6"] }
```

frank: The Go helper currently returns a []float64 mapped by index; we then create []Result{ID:i,Score:scores[i],Meta:meta[i]}. That fails when runtime reorders.

yuan: two bugs colliding: (1) the retry transport lost the per-batch `x-idempotency-key` after the async refactor so runtime treats retry as fresh and may reorder; (2) Go helper assumes positional stability and zips meta by index.

samir: also saw a vector-shape sanitizer gap. Our padVec was filling missing dims with `math.NaN()` in one codepath. The runtime coerced NaN->0 on some shards and threw on others which triggered fallback ordering.

anya: fix plan: (A) persist an `x-idempotency-key` UUID per batch and ensure transport re-uses it across retries; (B) change post-process to build id->score and id->meta maps from the server `result_ids` and reattach by id; fall back to index mapping only if server returns no ids and warn loudly. (C) tighten padVec: never emit NaN/undefined/null - throw error with context.

frank: agreed. For Go I'll sketch quick change: on response, if `result_ids` present -> map := map[string]float64; for i, id := range result_ids { map[id] = scores[i] }; then build results by iterating original ids and looking up map[id]. Emit helpful error if id missing.

samir: for padVec change: validate len(vec)==modelDim OR return error like `invalid_vector: id=doc-17 found_len=242 expected=256 missing=14 preview=[0.12,0.11,0.10,...]`. This avoids silent coercion.

yuan: CLI sampleapp also has a tiny example that intentionally omits idempotency header to keep the snippet short. We should add a one-line comment: `# in prod, set x-idempotency-key per batch to make retries idempotent`. Minimal, non-intrusive.

anya: I'll open issues and add tests: (DX-8110) persist idempotency across retry in Go transport, (DX-8111) batch post-process id->score mapping + unit tests (go/python/rust), (DX-8112) padVec strict validator + sampleapp smoke test (50 bursts).

frank: I'll draft a small PR in go-sdk: attach idempotency header, map by server-returned ids if present, and add a unit that stubs the runtime to return reordered `result_ids` on retry.

samir: For cross-language parity: add a parity harness that runs a fake runtime and ensures node/go/python produce same doc->score->meta mapping when runtime returns shuffled ids.

yuan: short-term mitigations: lower default batch retry to 1 for rerank in go/node/python; add quick CI smoke job in sampleapp that sends 100 batched rerank requests and asserts id sets + meta alignment.

dev-bot: Action items created: DX-8110, DX-8111, DX-8112. Reminders: include user-friendly error messages and a sampleapp README note about idempotency.

frank: PR draft: https://github.com/redwood-inference/go-sdk/pull/210 (draft) - adds idempotency persistence and id-based mapping. Assigning to @anya for review.

anya: thanks - will review tomorrow AM. Glad we caught this before GA of the 256 model. :thumbsup:
